Graph of the Derivative of a Smooth

Source: R/plot_smooth.R
plot_derivative.Rd

Selects the graph of the first or second derivative of the effect of a smooth of one numeric variable, with a confidence band.

Usage

plot_derivative(
  order = 1,
  level = 0.95,
  simultaneous = FALSE,
  n_sim = 10000,
  seed = NULL,
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(),
  n_grid = 200,
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

order

The order of the derivative, 1 or 2.

level

The confidence level of the band.

simultaneous

Whether the band is simultaneous over the grid.

n_sim

The number of draws that give the simultaneous critical value.

seed

NULL, or a single number that seeds the draws; the state of the random number generator is restored afterwards.

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance of the band.

n_grid

The number of points of the grid of the variable.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotDerivative object, inheriting from term_plot.

Details

The effect of the smooth is \(f(x) = X(x) b\), where \(X(x)\) is the row of the block of the term at \(x\) and \(b\) its coefficients, so that \(f^{(m)}(x) = X^{(m)}(x) b\) is linear in \(b\). The rows \(X^{(m)}(x)\) are obtained from the design of the term by one finite-difference stencil of order \(m\) and accuracy four, with the step and the weights of numericals7 (numericals7::fd_step(), numericals7::fd_weights()); near the ends of the range of the variable the nodes are shifted inside the range. The standard error of the derivative is the exact delta-method value \(\sqrt{X^{(m)}(x)\, V\, X^{(m)}(x)'}\), where \(V\) is the block of vcov.StatmodFit() for the coefficients of the term. The graph has the derivative with respect to the variable on the axis, on the scale of the link.

With simultaneous = FALSE the band is the derivative \(\pm z_{(1+\text{level})/2}\) standard errors. With simultaneous = TRUE the factor \(z\) is replaced by the level quantile of \(\max_x |X^{(m)}(x)\, e| / \mathrm{se}(x)\), where \(e\) is drawn n_sim times from \(N(0, V)\), so that the band covers the whole derivative over the grid with probability level (the simultaneous bands of Ruppert, Wand and Carroll). A smooth with a by factor is drawn as one curve for each level, each with its own critical value.

See also

plot_effect(), autoplot.StatmodFit()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(150))
dd$y <- sin(2 * pi * dd$x) + rnorm(150, sd = 0.3)
fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x), distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "s(x)", plot_type = plot_derivative(), data = dd)

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "s(x)",
                  plot_type = plot_derivative(order = 2, simultaneous = TRUE,
                                         n_sim = 2000, seed = 1),
                  data = dd)
